data.title: Enhancing CD8 T-cell memory by modulating fatty acid metabolism
data.authors: Pearce EL; Walsh MC; Cejas PJ; Harms GM; Shen H; Wang LS; Jones RG; Choi Y

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Mice with T-cell-specific TRAF6 deletion (CD4-cre), OT-I TCR-transgenic adoptive transfer, Listeria monocytogenes-OVA infection, EL4-OVA tumour vaccine model, and activated mouse CD8 T cells in vitro after IL-2 withdrawal
data.finding: Mice whose T cells lacked the adaptor protein TRAF6 mounted a normal effector CD8 T-cell response to Listeria infection, but the antigen-specific cells vanished during contraction and almost no memory cells formed. The TRAF6-deficient cells failed to activate AMPK and mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation when the growth factor IL-2 was withdrawn. Daily metformin restored fatty acid oxidation and memory formation, and also raised memory CD8 T-cell numbers in normal mice: in a tumour vaccine model 6 of 9 metformin-treated mice survived beyond day 33 against 1 of 8 controls. Daily rapamycin (1.5 mg/kg), used as a second drug that promotes fatty acid oxidation, likewise increased memory CD8 T-cell development and recall responses. Boundary: mouse only, one bacterial infection model and one transplantable tumour; the rapamycin arm is a secondary experiment and mTOR activity itself was not measured in these cells.
data.abstract_excerpt: CD8 T cells, which have a crucial role in immunity to infection and cancer, are maintained in constant numbers, but on antigen stimulation undergo a developmental program characterized by distinct phases encompassing the expansion and then contraction of antigen-specific effector (T(E)) populations, followed by the persistence of long-lived memory (T(M)) cells. Although this predictable pattern of CD8 T-cell responses is well established, the underlying cellular mechanisms regulating the transition to T(M) cells remain undefined.

extracted_findings.intervention: T-cell-specific TRAF6 deletion; daily metformin (250 mg/kg); daily rapamycin (1.5 mg/kg)
extracted_findings.target: CD8 T-cell fatty acid oxidation and memory formation
extracted_findings.effect: TRAF6 loss abolished CD8 memory formation; metformin or rapamycin increased memory CD8 T cells, and metformin improved anti-tumour vaccine protection
